analysis.title: Top Stories - Jack McKeon - 3 Nov 2026
key_insights: Chinese regulators told banks to hold off on company listings and large share sales to support the country's weak stock markets (FT).
China will raise the reserve requirement on FX deposits to reduce appreciation pressure on the yuan (SCMP).
The US arranged trilateral talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi next week to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. It is the first meeting of the three sides since February (FT).

The RBA raised its cash rate 25bp to 4.85%, an 18-year high and the fifth hike this year. The board voted 6-3 and dropped language saying it was willing to hike further, and Governor Bullock signaled a wait-and-see stance (BBG).
The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, one of a series of limited strikes carried out in recent weeks while President Trump spoke of a possible diplomatic deal (WSJ).

VP Vance said he was optimistic about a negotiated settlement with Iran. An Iranian official said the two sides remain far apart and Tehran threatened retaliatory strikes in the region and beyond (CNBC).
Nvidia is ordering its data center partners to reduce exposure to Chinese customers, which further limits China's ability to keep pace with US AI rivals (FT).
The US plans to ask NATO allies to put more money into a weapons-delivery program for Ukraine, possibly as soon as this month (BBG).
US-listed ETFs took in just over $200B in October, the second-largest monthly inflow in the dataset, bringing the year-to-date total to +$1.7T (H/T Chris Lucas).
Overnight data was mixed. Hong Kong retail sales and Q4 GDP beat, Swiss CPI rose above forecast, and Vietnam CPI was cooler than expected.
Heavy earnings day. Pre-market names include MPC, PFE, ADM, SYY, DD and YUM. After-market names include AMD, AMGN, SMCI, ANET, BKNG and AIG.
The US data calendar at 10:00 am ET has Sep JOLTS (est. 7164k, prior 7079k), Sep factory orders (est. 1.2%, prior 0.1%) and Sep final durable goods orders (est. 1.8%).

Rating changes were concentrated in two names. Lumentum got an upgrade at Raymond James (PT $1,328) and downgrades at B Riley (PT $770) and Stifel (PT $806). Marvell was cut at TD Cowen (PT $175) and BofA.
